hypotheses.title: Decorrelated Quarterly Foreign Currency Translation Adjustments and Volatility-Scaled Hedging
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Multinational companies reporting consistently positive after-tax foreign currency translation adjustments (fn_oth_income_loss_fx_transaction_and_tax_translation_adj_q) possess superior risk management infrastructure that protects international earnings against FX volatility. Evaluating quarterly reports over a 180-day semi-annual window (Alpha 11 architecture) or scaling against foreign operating income (fnd2_ebitfr) isolates operational treasury alpha. Blending with a 5-day weekly price reversal or volatility-scaled reversal overlay decorrelates the signal from existing 3-day reversal alphas (breaking self-correlation below 0.70) while optimizing turnover and lifting Fitness into the EXCELLENT tier.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if foreign exchange gains stem from unhedged speculative currency swings rather than disciplined risk management.

candidates.rationale: Candidate 1: 180-Day Semi-Annual TS Rank on Quarterly FX with 5-Day Weekly Reversal Overlay (Solves Fitness & Decorrelates)
Candidate 2: 1-Year Average Quarterly FX with Volatility-Scaled 5-Day Reversal Overlay (Breaks Self-Correlation < 0.70)
Candidate 3: Foreign Operating Hedging Ratio (Quarterly FX Translation normalized by Foreign EBIT fnd2_ebitfr) with 5-Day Reversal
